reasons: Deviation is correctly identified: Article XIII(b) caps only Licensor at one half of amounts paid (well below the six-month walk-away floor) and leaves Licensee (the client) uncapped, and the consequential-damages exclusion in (a) runs one way in Licensor's favour with no carve-outs — squarely within the rule's walk-away territory.

The redline reaches the preferred position: exclusion and cap made mutual ('either party'), basis reset to the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, an Excluded Claims definition covering confidentiality/data protection/security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement, and confirmation that Licensee's fee obligations are not capped damages.

Direction is client-favourable throughout: capping Licensee's previously unlimited exposure (including the Article XII indemnity), raising Licensor's illusory half-of-fees cap, and adding mutual protection without surrendering any existing Licensee right (narrowing 'Licensee or any third party' to 'the other party' is neutral-to-favourable).

Edits stay within the existing sentences of p0130; the single failed minimal-edit heuristic (0.816) corresponds to sub-clause (b), whose basis and mutuality had to be rewritten to implement the rule — an acceptable rule-driven rewrite. Adding 'Except for Excluded Claims' to the blanket IP-infringement disclaimer is a proportionate carve-out consistent with the rule's scope.

Comment is accurate, correctly characterises the one-way half-of-fees cap, states the playbook position (indemnities/confidentiality outside the cap, fees not damages) and offers the straight 12-month fallback in the required tone with the [Playbook] prefix.
